exampleAnswers.title: Computing Residuals Using the Regression Line Equation

question.text: Consider the data sets $x$ and $y$ of paired observations. The equation of the corresponding linear regression line for this data is \[ y=-1.5x+2. \] According to the model, what is the residual at $x=12$ if the actual value of $y$ corresponding to this value of $x$ is $-14?$
question.explanation:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

\[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \]

First, we compute the predicted value using our linear regression model:

\begin{align*} \widehat{y} &= -1.5x+2 \\[3pt] &= -1.5(12)+2 \\[3pt] &= -16 \end{align*}

Therefore, the residual is

\begin{align*} \textrm{Residual} &= \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \\[3pt] &= y-\widehat{y} \\[3pt] &= -14-(-16) \\[3pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

question.text: An antique broker has records about the value of an artwork $y$ (in thousands of dollars) at certain times $x$ (in decades) since the artwork was produced. The equation of the corresponding linear regression line for this data is \[ y=3.2x+4.5. \] What is the residual $5$ decades after the artwork was produced if the actual value of the artwork after $5$ decades is $\$23\,000?$
question.explanation:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

\[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \]

First, we compute the estimated value using our linear regression model:

\begin{align*} \widehat{y} &= 3.2x+4.5 \\[3pt] &= 3.2(5)+4.5 \\[3pt] &= 20.5 \end{align*}

As a result,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Residual} &= \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \\[3pt] &= y-\widehat{y} \\[3pt] &= 23 - 20.5 \\[3pt] &= 2.5. \end{align*}

Therefore, the residual is $\$2\,500.$

question.text: A veterinarian collects data on a puppy's height $y$ (in inches) at certain times $x$ (in months) since it was born. The equation of the corresponding linear regression line for this data is \[ y=2.2x+3.5. \] What is the residual after $5$ months if the actual height of the $5$-month old puppy is $15.5\, \mathrm{in}?$
question.explanation:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

\[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \]

First, we compute the estimated height using our linear regression model:

\begin{align*} \widehat{y} &= 2.2x+3.5 \\[3pt] &= 2.2(5)+3.5 \\[3pt] &= 14.5 \end{align*}

As a result,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Residual} &= \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \\[3pt] &= y-\widehat{y} \\[3pt] &= 15.5 - 14.5 \\[3pt] &= 1. \end{align*}

Therefore, the residual is $1\, \mathrm{in}.$

question.text:
The residual plot above was constructed after fitting a linear regression model on a set of bivariate numerical data $(x,y).$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. When $x=2,$ the regression equation overestimates the value of $y.$
  2. The residuals appear to be randomly scattered about the horizontal axis (there are no obvious trends).
  3. This linear regression is probably a good fit for the data.
question.explanation:
Let's examine the statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false. The residual equals the actual value minus the estimated value: \[ \textrm{Residual} = \text{Actual} - \textrm{Estimated} \] From the plot, the residual at $x=2$ is positive. So, we have that $\text{Actual} > \textrm{Estimated},$ and therefore the model underestimates (not overestimates) this data point.

  • Statement II is true. The plot shows that the residuals appear randomly scattered about the horizontal axis (there are no obvious trends).

  • Statement III is true. Since the residuals are close to $0$ and are randomly scattered above and below the horizontal axis, we can conclude that our regression line is probably a good fit for the given data.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
